cards.title: Boulders roll now
cards.text: Both of your ways are in: a turning picture and a sliding texture. Standing still, both are the old boulder.
cards.why: You asked for two ways to make the boulders roll, the same look as now, and a dirt trail. Each film puts the old ball and the two new ones side by side on the same path. Mark any part that's off.

parts.title: A: the turning picture
parts.text: The round picture turns over the way the ball rolls: what's on top goes over the front, what was underneath comes up the back. Works the same in every direction and round a turn, unlike a flat spin, which only looks right one way.

parts.title: B: the sliding texture
parts.text: A flat stone texture that repeats, cut out by the ball's outline, slides the way it rolls by the distance rolled. A fish-eye makes the middle move faster than the edges, so it reads round.

parts.title: Same look as now
parts.text: Both are made from the old boulder's own picture: same colours, chips, moss and outline. The light, highlight and shade stay put while the stone turns under them. Standing still, all three match.

parts.title: Yeti's ball
parts.text: The two thin lines that went round it are gone; its own picture turns instead. Gone too: the fat dark ring it flashed while growing as it rolled.

parts.title: Dirt trail
parts.text: Dust puffs, small clods and faint scuffs behind a rolling boulder; snow spray and clumps behind a snowball. More the faster it goes; almost nothing at a push, nothing standing still.

parts.title: In real fights
parts.text: The same troll fight and yeti fight three times: before, A, B. The fights play out the same; only the drawing changes.

parts.title: Try it in game
parts.text: Settings, Dev: Rolling boulders (sliding texture, turning picture, or before) and a switch for the dirt trail.

cards.title: Which way to keep?
cards.text: Rolling in a line they look alike. A is truer in tight turns; B costs a bit less to draw.
cards.why: B is your sliding texture: four stone patches, so more variety as it rolls, and a quarter to a third cheaper per boulder. A really turns the ball, so on a tight turn the picture twists the way a real ball does. Both are well under a millisecond a boulder.
cards.pick: B, the sliding texture. It's on by default; A is one tap away in Settings, Dev.

cards.title: Moss rolls off the top
cards.text: Once it has rolled, the moss cap can be anywhere on the ball, and its other side shows smaller moss patches.
cards.why: A ball that really rolls can't keep its moss on top. The old picture only had one side, so the other side is new: the same chips and moss, smaller, in the same colours.
cards.pick: Keep it: that's what rolling looks like.

cards.title: One dust colour
cards.text: The dust is the game's usual pale dust on every floor. It could take the floor's colour instead.
cards.why: The game's other dust (dashes, landings) is the same pale colour everywhere, so the trail matches it. Sand-coloured dust in the Dunes or dark dust in the Ember Deep would be a small change.
cards.pick: Keep one colour, like the rest of the game's dust.
